recommendation: Keep the human-review audit unless someone with Jira attachment access can recover Archive.zip. If recovered, compare the FHIR Infrastructure QA report entries against current build-scoped source and create precise follow-up fixes only for remaining substantive discrepancies.
issue_request: FHIR-17603 is a Published/Persuasive technical-correction issue for the FHIR Infrastructure work group. It asks editors to use the attached Archive.zip QA review files from an earlier QA process to check that updates had been applied; Jira records an Auto-approved resolution, related page FHIR-core-many, applied-for version R5, no clarifying comments, and attachment 15599.
initial_application: No current source reference, git commit message, or history search result before this AutoFHIR run explicitly mentions FHIR-17603, GF#17603, #17603, or tracker 17603. Historical FHIR Infrastructure source changes and QA-era edits exist around August-December 2018 for Bundle, CapabilityStatement, ImplementationGuide, OperationDefinition, Parameters, Subscription, and related artifacts, but none can be tied to the Archive.zip entries or to this Jira key.
additional_context: The actionable details appear to be only in Jira attachment 15599, and both the secure attachment URL and REST attachment-content URL returned HTTP 403 in this environment. Current source/fhir.ini lists active FHIR Infrastructure artifacts using the fhir work-group code, but no current source index identifies the archive entries. Checked-in qa/*.docx files are historical review documents and are not referenced by source/fhir.ini or checked build files found in this reconciliation. Jira search shows a family of separate QA report issues for different work groups, and sibling audits already on the combined branch reached the same human-review conclusion where their archives were inaccessible. Zulip and Confluence searches found only an automated tracker notification, a 2023 FHIR-I status-list mention, and a 2022 WGM minute saying to unassign the issue from Lloyd; none clarify the requested QA changes.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. An empty human-review audit commit was published on the combined branch because there is no bounded, verifiable source location or semantic correction to apply without the archive contents.
